text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 5 in history:
1355 - Charles IV was crowned in Rome as Holy Roman Emperor.
1513 - Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian, Henry VIII of England, Ferdinand of Aragon and Pope Leo X signed the Treaty of Mechlin by which an alliance was formed for a joint invasion of France.
1588 - Thomas Hobbes, English philosopher, born. He developed his ideas in "Leviathan, or the Matter, Form, Power of a Commonwealth" (1651).
1614 - The second parliament of James I began sitting. Known as the Addled Parliament, it was dissolved on June 7 without passing a single bill.
1614 - In America, Pocahontas, daughter of King Powahatan, married the farmer John Rolfe in the church at Jamestown.

1724 - Giovanni Jacopo Casanova de Seingalt, Italian lover and adventurer, born. During his life he was a seminarian, a secretary to a cardinal, a Venetian ensign, an abbe, a gambler, an alchemist, a violinist, a spy, and a librarian.

1794 - Georges Jacques Danton, French revolutionary leader, was guillotined for treason. He tried to temper the Revolutionary Tribunal's severity, which he himself had set up and by which he was ultimately sentenced.
1827 - Joseph Lister, British surgeon and scientist, born; the pioneer of antiseptics, he revolutionised modern surgery.
1881 - In South Africa, the Treaty of Pretoria was signed by the British and the Boers, recognising the independence of the Transvaal.
1900 - Spencer Tracy, U.S. actor, born. He was the first actor to win an Academy Award in successive years, for his performances in "Captains Courageous" (1937) and "Boy's Town" (1938).
1901 - Melvyn Douglas, U.S. actor of stage and screen, born as Melvyn Edouard Hesselberrg; famed for his appearence with Greta Garbo in "Ninotchka".
1908 - Bette Davis, U.S. film actress, born. She won Oscars for "Dangerous" and "Jezebel" but was perhaps best remembered for her role in the film "All About Eve".
1916 - Gregory Peck, U.S. film actor, born. Best known for his role as a liberal Southern lawyer in "To Kill a Mockingbird" for which he won an Oscar.
1941 - In World War Two, Allied forces re-captured Addis Ababa in Ethiopia.
1951 - Julius and Ethel Rosenberg were sentenced to death by Judge Kaufman for giving atomic secrets away to the Russians.
1955 - In England, Winston Churchill resigned as Prime Minister.
1964 - Douglas MacArthur, U.S. general and Pacific commander in World War Two, died
1964 - In Bhutan, while the King was in Europe, Prime Minister Jigme Dorji was assassinated. He was succeeded by his brother until the King's return.
1970 - Count Carl von Spreti, West German ambassador to Guatemala, was found murdered six days after his kidnapping by guerrillas.
1975 - Chiang Kai-shek, Chinese military and political leader, died; Chiang fled to Taiwan after his Nationalist forces lost the Chinese civil war against Mao Zedong in 1949,
1982 - The first ships of the British Royal Navy Task Force left Portsmouth for the Falkland Islands after they had been taken over by Argentina.
1984 - Sir Arthur "Bomber" Harris, chief of British Bomber Command during World War Two, died.
1989 - The Polish government legalised the Solidarity union, and introduced democratic measures into the political system.
1992 - Suada Dilberovic, a 24-year-old Croat medical student shot and killed by a sniper on the Vrbania bridge in Sarajevo, became the first woman casualty of the war in Bosnia.
1995 - Israel launched its first spy satellite. The Ofek 3 was put into space by an Israeli Shavit rocket.
1996 - In Canada, an estranged husband opened fire on guests preparing for a wedding killing nine people in Vernon, British Columbia. He then killed himself in Canada's second-worst mass shooting.
